en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who is saying, ‘Upon me is a vow’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with anything until he names the vow and is saying, ‘Upon me is a Fast for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, or a charity, or freeing (a slave), or an offering of a gift. And if the man says, ‘I gift this food’, so this is not with anything, but rather the camel is an offering’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Afi ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who says that there is a vow, a commitment on him. He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not have any valid effect until he says, “There is fasting, or paying charity, or freeing a slave, or offering an animal offering.” If a man says, “I give this food as an offering,” it is not valid, because only a camel or so can become an animal offering.’”
